audit_item:
Header Clamp - Check for full compression of lock washer. Bolt should be tightened to manufacturers specification. 
Spine Clamp Hardware - Check for full compression of lock washer. Bolt should be tightened to manufacturers specification.
Truss Splice Plate - Check for full compression of lock washer. Bolt should be tightened to manufacturers specification.
Splice Joint - All bolt should be in contact with track. Check track for alignment and that  wheel rolling surface is flash.
Hoist Trolley - Check clevis pin. Check cotter pin. (Cotter pin should be fully wrapped around clevis pin) Check clevis pin bolt and hardware.
End Stops - Check for full compression of lock washer. If thru bolt is exposed, replace end stops.
Vacuum Hoist Clamp - Check for full compression of lock washer.
Wheels - Check for cracks, puts, and grooves: all of these increase pull force. If any of these conditions exists. wheel should be replaced.
Aluminum Bridge Hardware -  Check that lock washers are compressed and nuts tightened to torque specification. Ensure sheer lug hardware is required position and tight.
End Trucks - Check for proper clamping hardware attachment. Ensure correct position on bridge to match specified cantilevers. Inspect end truck wheels following instruction for wheel above. Make sure body of is free of any bent materials, cracked or broken welds. Check overall condition of tubes. Examine support for bent materials, cracked or broken welds. Inspect hardware attaching end truck support tubes. Check wheel plate attachment bolts for any wear and make sure the nylock nut is still in the correct position.

1. check hydraulic fluid
2. Clean all debris from the vicinity of floor and pit mounted units in order to avoid interference with the lift mechanism or roller.
3. Check for presence and proper seating of all snap rings and clips on all axles, cylinder and rolls.
4. Check rollers , pins and bushing for any signs of wear such as flat spots, missing fasteners or dislodged bearing material.
5. Check the hydraulic fittings for cracks or leaks and clean up any weepage on or beneath the cylinder.
6. Check hoses and electrical lines for abrasions or other abuse and check for snug connections.
7. Operate the unit and check for any abnormal noise or vibrations.
8. Check all safety devices on the unit such as the condition of the pleated bellows or smooth operation of the electric toe guard.
